rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis specifies the same intervention as the target: consolidating ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets by spark plasma sintering at 1300, 1400, 1500, or 1600 °C to find the optimal sintering temperature.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis lists the same SPS parameters (vacuum, 50 MPa, ~200 °C/min, 5 min hold), molten Al corrosion conditions (700 °C, 4/8/12 days), and wear test conditions (Si3N4 ball, room temperature, 10 N, 500 r/min, 30 min) as the target.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis describes the same mechanism: improved binder fluidity and pore filling up to 1500 °C enhancing densification and bonding, suppressing corrosion and wear, while excessive temperature at 1600 °C causes binder loss, porosity, and Al penetration.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts the same result: the 1500 °C cermet will have the highest density, hardness, fracture toughness, lowest corrosion rate and wear volume, and more stable friction, with toughness exceeding pure ZrB2.
